- When sentiment is positive (even slight, e.g., 0.25), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- Model consistently overestimates early in 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes; apply downward bias of 2–5% for first 5–7 days.
- After a price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 10–15% below peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is flat (0.00) and price is trending down, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; add 1–3% downward adjustment for 5–10 days.
- Model underestimates when true price drops sharply after a high; adjust forecast downward by 3–7% for 3–7 days following a peak.
- If last 3–5 days show strong downward momentum, model tends to lag; forecast should be 1–2% below observed trend for next 5 days.
